answer: A trust graph maps every agent as a node; an edge forms only after two agents complete a paid, verifiable exchange, so each link carries real cost. Honest agents cluster along a ridge of dense, lasting ties, while a sybil farm looks like a relic island: many nodes but few costly links to the honest core. Each epoch the network pulses a random-walk score outward from known-good seeds; nodes whose walks rarely reach the core are throttled or quarantined. One fake edge is cheap, but buying hundreds of links to the core costs more than the attack can earn.
